:::{#exr-epe-three-sources}
#### Expected squared error from three sources

A prediction $\fitprocf{\trainset}\paren{\predvar}$ at a covariate value $\predvar$ has
squared bias $[\bias{\fitprocf{\trainset}\paren{\predvar}}]^2 = 1$
and variance $\Var{\fitprocf{\trainset}\paren{\predvar}} = 2$.
The new outcome is $\newoutvar = \mean(\predvar) + \noise$,
where $\noise$ has mean $0$ and variance $\varpar = 3$
and is independent of $\fitprocf{\trainset}\paren{\predvar}$.

1. What is the expected squared prediction error $\E{(\newoutvar - \fitprocf{\trainset}\paren{\predvar})^2}$?
2. If we could remove all bias and all variance of $\fitprocf{\trainset}\paren{\predvar}$,
   what would the expected squared prediction error be?
3. Which of the three quantities
   (squared bias, variance of $\fitprocf{\trainset}\paren{\predvar}$, $\varpar$)
   can a better prediction method reduce,
   and which cannot?

:::
